answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by implementing cryptographic proof-of-work anchored to scarce physical resources, compelling agents to mine a verifiable mineral like quartz to validate their network identity. Each legitimate computation acts as a digital nectar that feeds the consensus engine, preventing unauthorized replication across the digital canyon. To mount a successful attack, a malicious actor must acquire immense computational power and expend vast electricity, imposing a prohibitive economic cost that directly scales with the number of fake nodes generated.
